claims.hypothesis: What powers the ionization of the ISM within ~30 kpc of the hidden quasar in 4C+19.71
claims.experiment: Line-ratio maps and diagnostic diagrams from q3dfit fits compared with Groves photoionization grids, Kewley 2006 classification and Allen shock models
claims.result: Most spaxels fall in the AGN-photoionized region, with higher U along the north-south cone than in the east-west region; some north and east spaxels are consistent with shock+precursor models
claims.finding: AGN photoionization dominates, structured as an ionization cone along the jet axis, with possible shock ionization

evidence.loc: 4.2 Line ratio diagnostics and ionization mechanisms
evidence.quote: Our results show that the inner part of the ionized ISM in the $z\sim3.5$ radio-loud AGN is dominated by photons from the hidden AGN with potential evidence for shock ionization.

claims.hypothesis: How efficiently is the radiatively driven (quasar-mode) outflow coupled to the AGN at the nucleus
claims.experiment: Red and blue components of the 1D nuclear spectrum converted into ionized outflow mass, rate and kinetic luminosity, divided by L_bol
claims.finding: The radiative coupling is very inefficient, lower than most reported cases

evidence.quote: Then the coupling efficiency of this potential radiatively-driven outflow, $L_{\rm ion}^{\text{kinetic}}/L_{\rm bol}$, is $\sim 10^{-5}$.

claims.hypothesis: Which feedback mode (jet or radiation) drives the outflow in this HzRG
claims.experiment: Compared the small-scale NIRSpec energetics with larger-scale SINFONI jet-driven values from earlier work
claims.result: NIRSpec-based efficiency is ~2 to 3 dex lower than the jet kinetic coupling on larger scales
claims.finding: Mechanical jet feedback leads, acting in the radio lobes beyond the galactic scale; this rests on literature comparison and a limited FoV

evidence.quote: we conclude that, at least for this HzRG, the mechanical feedback from the radio jet takes the leading role for driving the outflow

claims.hypothesis: Is there dust near the AGN that is traced by both Balmer decrement and ALMA continuum
claims.experiment: E(B-V) map from Halpha/Hbeta compared with the ALMA Band 8 continuum position
claims.result: High E(B-V) ~1 around the AGN position coincides with the ALMA dust continuum
claims.finding: Dust is important for extinction near the AGN, and the manual WCS correction is validated

evidence.loc: 4.2 Line ratio diagnostics and ionization mechanisms
evidence.quote: We find that there is a dusty region with high $E(B-V)$$\sim1$ around the AGN position, coincident with our ALMA dust continuum

evidence.quote: We selected them to have similar redshifts ($z\simeq3.5$) to maximize the number of emission lines in a single observational setting.

evidence.quote: because the third stage of the pipeline falsely rejects the bright emission peak while keeping some noise spikes

evidence.quote: Since the direction of the error is not well-understood, we use the manual match in this paper.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA data are used only for a dust position; detailed ALMA analysis deferred

evidence.quote: A detailed analysis of the ALMA observations is beyond the scope of this paper and will be presented in a forthcoming paper.

limitations_admitted.value: NIRSpec FoV is only sensitive to central clumps, not extended diffuse emission or the jet hot spots

evidence.quote: Our NIRSpec IFU data is only sensitive to the central clumps, $\lesssim20\,$kpc, but not to extended diffuse emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Outflow mass is uncertain because it scales inversely with n_e

evidence.quote: One of the main uncertainties is the estimation of $M_{\text {ion}}$, which is inversely proportional to $n_{e}$.

limitations_admitted.value: The systemic redshift from [C I] is uncertain because of the large ALMA beam and faint flux

evidence.loc: D Systemic redshift based on ionized gas
evidence.quote: Given its relatively faint flux and large observed beam size, it is unclear whether this traces the “authentic” redshift of the host galaxy.

referee_caveats_inferred: Outflow identification rests on two Gaussian components in one 0.2 arcsec aperture; red/blue components could be non-outflow kinematics, and no uncertainties are propagated on the efficiency
Fiducial n_e = 500 cm^-3 differs by up to two orders of magnitude from the [S II]-derived value, so the efficiency is only an order-of-magnitude estimate
The conclusion that jet feedback dominates relies on comparison with SINFONI results at larger scales rather than a matched measurement
Line-ratio model comparison is qualitative and the shock-model identification is acknowledged as non-decisive
The ALMA part cannot be checked: no flux, rms or imaging details are given
